# Sivirājacariya (Cp 8)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sivirājacariya* (Cp 8 or Cariyāpiṭaka 1.8) is a canonical Pali text found in the *Cariyāpiṭaka*, the fifteenth book of the *Khuddaka Nikāya* [Ohnuma 1997; SuttaCentral]. Positioned as the eighth narrative in the collection, it forms part of the opening set of stories illustrating the Bodhisatta's perfection of the virtue of giving (*dānapāramitā*) [Bareau; Wood 2005]. Rather than being an expansive prose narrative, it presents a concise, versified recounting of the well-known legend of King Sivi, narrated in the first-person voice by the Buddha himself [Ohnuma 1997; Ohnuma 2007]. In this account, King Sivi resolves to give an unprecedented gift to a supplicant and bestows both of his eyes upon an old, blind brahmin who is actually the deity Sakka in disguise [Ohnuma 2000; Ohnuma 2007]. The narrative in the *Cariyāpiṭaka* concludes abruptly with the completion of the bodily gift, omitting the subsequent restoration of the king's eyes through an Act of Truth found in fuller versions [Ohnuma 1997; Ohnuma 2007].

**Sources**

- [Bareau] André Bareau, Les récits canoniques du Cariyāpiṭaka et les Jātaka Pāli — Supplies the place of Sivi-rāja-Cariyam as story number 8 in the list of Cariyāpiṭaka texts.
- [Wood 2005] Leela Aditi Wood, Buddha and the Shape of Belief: Indic Visual Jatakamalas, vol. 1 (2005) — Discusses the Cariyāpiṭaka's dānapāramitā section and its relationship with the Jātakamālā's Śibi Jātaka.
- [Ohnuma 2007] Reiko Ohnuma, Head, Eyes, Flesh and Blood: Giving Away the Body in Indian Buddhist Literature (2007) — Summarizes the narrative content of Cariyāpiṭaka 1.8 (giving of both eyes to Sakka in disguise, first-person narration, omission of eye restoration).
- [Ohnuma 2000] Reiko Ohnuma, Internal and External Opposition to the Bodhisattva's Gift of His Body (2000) — Quotes the Bodhisattva's declaration in Cariyāpiṭaka 1.8 regarding giving an excellent gift never given before.
- [Ohnuma 1997] Reiko Ohnuma, Dehadāna: The Gift of the Body in Indian Buddhist Narrative Literature (Ph.D. dissertation, 1997) — Notes that Sivirājacariyam is a brief versified first-person account of Sivijātaka (Jātaka No. 499) in the Khuddaka Nikāya, concluding with the making of the gift.
